note: Names, descriptions and grades match the official PlayStation trophy list exactly. Guides are original, written for this guide from the official descriptions. GTA VI is unreleased, so any step the description only implies is labelled as implied, not verified, and no specific location is stated as fact without a cited source.

trophies.guide: The platinum. It unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no separate task. Work through the roadmap in order: story first, then side missions, collectibles, activities, combat and crime, and the economy cleanup last. The final gate is usually the 100% completion trophy, so track that percentage from the start.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. This is the first story mission, so it unlocks naturally as you play — there is nothing to prepare for and nothing to miss. If you are following the story, this is the first trophy you will earn.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end. Chapter trophies unlock on completion of the chapter's final mission, so just keep following the story. Nothing in a chapter trophy is missable: finishing the chapter is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its end. Like the other chapter trophies, this unlocks when the chapter's last mission is complete. Use Chapter 2 to start the side content that opens up around it — stranger missions and activities count toward later trophies, and doing them as they appear saves backtracking.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its end. The name points to Vice City itself, and the chapter trophy unlocks on the final mission of the chapter. Keep an eye on the missable watchlist during this stretch: the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) need your partner beside you, so take those chances when the story puts you together.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); Rockstar Games — GTA VI official site

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 4 to its end — the last chapter trophy before the finale. By now the map should be largely open; if any collectible or activity trophy is close to done, finish it before the final mission so the endgame is pure cleanup rather than a long grind.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. This is the gold story trophy and the natural end of Stage 1 of the roadmap. Before you start the finale, check the missable watchlist one last time: anything that needs a story-only moment should be done first, because post-game free roam may not bring those moments back.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies unlock when the mission ends, win or lose on the first try — a failed attempt costs nothing but a retry, and the mission can be replayed. Just play the story in order and this unlocks on its own.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games are usually the big set-pieces of a chapter, and this trophy is simply for finishing it. No special approach is needed: complete the mission and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Another mission-completion trophy: play the mission to the end and it unlocks. The title suggests a family thread in the story, but the requirement is only the mission itself.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Finishing the mission is the whole requirement. Headliners is one of the named story missions with its own trophy, so it is easy to track: when the mission appears in your story log, play it and this trophy is done.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. The mission name ties directly to the airport, and the trophy is for completion only. Note the separate free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can, which is also about the airport — do not confuse the two.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); Rockstar Games — GTA VI official site

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a larger military or raid-style mission, but the trophy itself asks only for completion. Play it when it appears in the story and it unlocks.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own completion tracker. In GTA games this percentage is made of story missions, side missions, collectibles, activities and a few hidden tasks — not of every trophy. The practical route: finish the story, clear every stranger strand, collect everything, and check the in-game stats page for the remaining percentage points. This is the last trophy for most players and the real gate before the platinum.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy guide (community)

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts. Stunts in GTA games are jumps, near-misses, long air time and two-wheel driving — anything the game flashes as a stunt. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so it builds up on its own if you drive fast and take jumps. To grind it deliberately, use a fast car on long straight roads and a stunt jump you can repeat: each clean landing counts. The game is unreleased, so the exact list of what counts as a stunt is not yet confirmed — the number 250 is from the official description.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type once. The official description does not name the types, so the full list is unconfirmed until release — the trailer and official site show fishing, golf, bowling, arcade games, shooting ranges, drone racing and more. Practical approach: open the map and the activities menu and try each icon once; keep a note of which you have done. This trophy is cheap if you sample activities as you travel instead of leaving them all for the end.
trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); Rockstar Games — GTA VI Trailer 2

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge. Shooting ranges in GTA games test accuracy and speed with a set of weapons, each challenge having bronze, silver and gold score thresholds. Work through the challenges one weapon at a time, learn each course's targets, and repeat until gold. The number of challenges is not stated in the official description, so no count is given here. The range is a good early grind: it also sharpens the aim you need for Combat Focus and the heist missions.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every race location. Drone races are flown through checkpoints, and each location has its own course. Learn the course layout on a practice run, then race to win — the trophy needs a win at each location, not just a finish. The number of locations is not stated in the official description, so check the map for Top Fun icons and clear them one by one.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The key word is different: winning the same race 20 times does not count. Race variety comes from the game's race types — street races, off-road, boat and air races are all likely on offer — so work through the race list and win each one once. If a race is hard, upgrade the vehicle for that race type first; a win in a slow car is a grind, a win in a tuned car is a lap.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named fishing rival, so this is a head-to-head challenge rather than free fishing. The official description names no location, so the exact spot is unconfirmed until release — look for the fishing challenge marker and Cal's name when it appears. Fishing challenges in GTA games are usually about total weight or a target catch in a time limit, so bring the best rod and bait you have and focus on the big catches.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game. Arcade cabinets are found in arcades and bars around Leonida; walk up to one and play it through to the end. Any arcade game counts, so pick the one you find easiest. This is one of the cheapest trophies in the list — do it the first time you pass an arcade.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's last mission. Andy is one of the stranger contacts with a mission strand: take his missions as they appear on the map and follow the strand to its end. Stranger strands usually unlock in order, so if Andy's next mission is not showing, play more story first. The final mission of the strand is the trophy.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's last mission. Like Andy's strand, Kenton's missions appear as stranger missions and must be played in order. Keep returning to Kenton's marker between story missions until the strand ends — the trophy pops on the final mission's completion.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's last mission. Billy's strand is another stranger-mission chain: play each mission as it unlocks and the final one earns the trophy. If a strand stalls, it usually needs more story progress, so keep playing the main missions and check back.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands. Strangers are the '?' contacts scattered across Leonida — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret all have strands, and there are more. Each strand is a short chain of missions; finishing a chain counts as one. The five named contacts above cover five of the eight, so find three more stranger strands on the map and finish them too. This is a silver trophy and a good reason to explore the whole state, not just Vice City.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's last mission. Randy's strand follows the same pattern as the other stranger contacts: missions unlock in order, and the trophy comes with the final one. Play the strand when its marker appears and do not leave it half-finished — strands are easiest done in one sitting while you remember the thread.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's last mission. Tyrone is another stranger contact with a mission chain. Complete his missions in order until the final one. The name hints at a car or spinning theme, but the requirement is only the final mission — play the strand through and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet scenic locations — beaches, hilltops, parks — marked on the map once found. Visit each one and use the meditate prompt. The official description gives no count, so no number is stated here: work through the map region by region and tick spots off as you find them. This pairs naturally with the exploration trophy, since both reward covering the whole state.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's strand is a hunting one: he asks for a specific animal, and the trophy is for bringing it down. Unique animals in GTA games are usually one specific creature in one specific area, and the exact animal and location are not named in the official description, so they are unconfirmed until release. When Bret's mission starts, follow the tracking clues in the mission itself — it will lead you to the animal.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida, grouped into sets — finishing a set means finding every card in it. The official description does not say how many cards are in a set or how many sets exist, so no card count is stated here. Collect cards as you explore and keep a checklist; card locations are the kind of thing the community maps within days of release, and this guide's source list points to where those maps will appear.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy guide (community)

trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the game's photo or social-sharing feature — the name plays on winking at the camera. The requirement is 100 different locations, so variety matters: take the shot at landmarks, beaches, neighbourhoods and viewpoints across Leonida rather than repeating one spot. Work it into your exploration: whenever you reach a new area, WAiNK It before you leave.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives — stunt jumps, time trials, photo spots, and similar tasks scattered across Leonida — and they are counted cumulatively. Do them as you find them rather than saving them for the end: 50 is a large number, and the ones near your route are free progress. The in-game challenges menu shows which are done, so use it as your checklist.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it. MISSABLE RISK: this needs your partner present, and partner availability is story-gated — take the chance while the story keeps you together. To build heat fast, commit crimes in a busy area; to lose it, break line of sight and hide until the stars flash and clear. A quiet back road or water escape works better than a shootout, and your partner must survive the escape with you.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the level must stay active across all three robberies. MISSABLE RISK: like Hot Together, this needs your partner, so do it while the story has you together. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, hit each one quickly, and keep moving between them. If the wanted level clears between robberies, the chain breaks and you start over.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery means getting into or scanning a vehicle type you have not found before — the count is by vehicle model, not by individual cars. Drive everything you see: traffic cars, trucks, boats, bikes and aircraft all count toward the total. New areas bring new vehicles, so this grows naturally with exploration; if you stall near the end, check which vehicle classes you have never driven.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down five enemies during one use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-aim or precision-aim mode: activate it when five or more enemies are in front of you, then drop all five before it ends. The easiest setup is a mission or shootout with a group of enemies clustered together — wait until they are grouped, trigger Focus, and work through them fast. Missing one means retrying, so pick a fight with plenty of targets.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in an unscheduled way — the description's joke is that you take a plane (or another aircraft) without a ticket or a flight plan. The exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description, so the precise method is unconfirmed until release; the plain reading is to steal an aircraft at VCIA and take off. Try it in free roam with a fast plane and a clear runway, and expect airport security to object.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke about Rhino tanks: this trophy involves the Rhino tank. The official description does not say whether you must steal one, drive one, survive one or destroy one, so the exact trigger is unconfirmed until release. The sensible read is to get into a Rhino — tanks appear at military sites and at high wanted levels in GTA games — and the trophy should pop on entry or on your first use of it. Check the community guide sources in the source matrix once the game is out for the confirmed trigger.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy guide (community)

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the requirement: get in, take the goods and get out before any alarm or witness raises the alert. Plan the approach — enter when the store is quiet, avoid cameras and staff sightlines, and leave before the police are called. If you are spotted, the attempt fails; leave and try again. This is a clean-stealth trophy, so patience beats speed.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault robbery needs an entry plan and an escape plan: get in, crack or open the vault, grab the cash, and break away cleanly before the police close in. A fast getaway car parked nearby and a planned route out of the area make each robbery far easier. The count is cumulative, so you can do one vault, escape, and come back for the next later.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida; intercept one, stop it, take the cash and get away. The classic GTA approach is to block the truck with your own vehicle, deal with the guards, blow or force the rear doors, then escape before the wanted level builds. One clean robbery and escape is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida. The state is divided into named areas, and the trophy unlocks when you have visited them all. Drive the map systematically — coast, countryside, swamps, small towns and Vice City itself — rather than fast-travelling everywhere, since fast travel may not register an area. This pairs with the meditation spots, the WAiNK It locations and the vehicle discoveries: one thorough road trip covers several trophies at once. The official description gives no area count, so none is stated here.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); Rockstar Games — GTA VI official site

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Gangs run their own illicit businesses — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling spots — and each gang's operation is a robbery target. Work through the gangs one at a time: find an operation, rob it, and move to the next gang. The official description does not name the gangs or their number, so no count is stated here; the in-game map and gang intel will show which operations remain.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail at a bar or beach spot with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a small flavour trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find a bar with a view of the water, and order a cocktail. Ocean Beach is Vice City's beachfront, so look for beach bars along the strip. It costs almost nothing and takes a minute — do it the first time you are in the area.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); Rockstar Games — GTA VI official site

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, in the style of the classic GTA showroom escape. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or drive one in, then floor it through the front window. The trophy is about the exit, so the smash itself is the trigger; expect a wanted level and a repair bill afterwards.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. Go to that specific alley — the name is in the description, so it is a real location in the game — and play a game of bowling through to the end. Follow-through is the bowling term for completing your throw, so the trophy is about playing properly rather than just walking in. One full game should do it.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Build a partnership with mass appeal. The description is vague, and no detail is given in the official list, so the exact trigger is unconfirmed until release. The plain reading is a social or follower milestone tied to the game's partnership or social-media system — Lucia and Jason's partnership, or a business partnership that grows an audience. Treat this as a wait-for-release trophy: watch the community guide sources in the source matrix for the confirmed method rather than guessing.
trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy guide (community)

trophies.guide: Make choices over the course of the game. The description counts choices — decisions in missions and story moments — and the trophy unlocks once you have made enough of them. MISSABLE RISK: choices in a story are finite, so take every decision point seriously and do not rush past dialogue options; a skipped choice may not come back. The exact number of choices needed is not stated in the official description, so no count is given here. Play the story attentively and this should unlock before the finale.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second attempt at something. The description points to failing once and then succeeding — a retry trophy. The most likely trigger is a mission or challenge failed once and then passed, which happens naturally during play; if it has not popped by the end of the story, deliberately fail a short mission or challenge once and then complete it. The exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description, so this is an informed reading, not a verified method.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The description is the classic GTA easter-egg trophy: a UFO, a ghost, a cryptid or another weird event somewhere in Leonida. MISSABLE RISK: if the event is a one-off random encounter, it may be easy to walk past and hard to find again — keep an eye out while exploring remote areas at night. The exact event is not named in the official description, so the specific trigger is unconfirmed until release; the community guide sources in the source matrix will name it once players find it.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list (via Exophase); PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy guide (community)

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee weapon while driving by. A melee drive-by means attacking from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon — a bat or similar — rather than a gun. Find a pedestrian, drive past slowly, and swing as you pass. It takes timing more than force; a slow pass on a quiet street is easier than a fast one in traffic.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty cash earned from robberies and heists; your contacts clean it for a cut. The count is cumulative, so keep feeding marked bills to your contacts whenever you have them rather than hoarding them. This is a long grind that runs alongside the robbery trophies — every bank vault and armored truck adds to the total.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Any shop spending counts — clothes, weapons, car mods, food — and the total is cumulative across the whole game. You will spend a large part of this naturally on weapons and vehicle upgrades for the story; if you are short at the end, buy the most expensive items you still need rather than wasting cash. Track the total in the in-game stats if it is shown there.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in Leonida. Garages are purchasable properties that store your vehicles; each one costs money, so this is a late-game purchase once your cash is healthy. The official description does not say how many garages there are, so no count is stated here. Check the property or real-estate listings in-game for the full list and buy them one by one — owning them also makes the vehicle-collection trophies easier.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle-delivery app: register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat for ten different vehicles. Use the cheapest or most common vehicles you already own — ten registrations is quick once you know the app's menu. This is a cheap endgame trophy; do it while buying garages, since the two go together.
trophies.name: On the Spot
